thread:
emily: Observed a spike of 502/504s for api.prod originating in us-west-2b about 3m ago. Route53 health checks for the us-west-2b endpoint are flapping and weighted routing is oscillating. Customers hitting US-West are seeing intermittent failures.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created INC-2026-0421-usw2b-egress — paging @sam (oncall-sre). Auto-collected metrics: 502 rate 8%, p50 latency +200ms. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0421
oncall-bot: Paging: @sam is on call for incidents in #incidents.
sam: I got the page, taking lead. Setting P0. Any recent deploys or scaling events?
jordan: we pushed a canary to api-deploy ~3m ago (small config tweak). Rolling that back now.
jordan: running: ```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/api --to-revision=2
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api -o wide
```
yuki: I'm seeing target group churn in ELB: multiple targets in us-west-2b go OutOfService then re-register. ELB access logs show backend TLS handshake timeouts and some connection resets.
claire: Route53 health-check id hc-0a1b2c is flipping between healthy/unhealthy. TTL is 60s so routing shifts quickly — looks like weighted routing is bouncing traffic between AZs.
sam: Temp mitigation plan: 1) slow down Route53 failover sensitivity (increase failure threshold), 2) move weight away from affected us-west-2b targets, 3) scale up healthy targets in other AZs, 4) rollback canary (in progress).
emily: Applying Route53 change to increase failure threshold and pause automated failover: ```bash
aws route53 update-health-check --health-check-id hc-0a1b2c --failure-threshold 8
```
(emily: command succeeded, change propagated)
jordan: reverting canary finished. Observability: error rate dropping from 8% -> 1.8% over last 2m.
yuki: also increased target group deregistration delay and connection draining to 120s to reduce churn while backends stabilize. Ran: ```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234 --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=120
```
claire: Posting a shortstatus to status.redwood.ai: "We are mitigating an elevated error rate affecting some US-West customers. Traffic is being shifted away from the impacted AZ while we stabilize backends."
sam: Good. Jordan, can you confirm no further unhealthy target storms?
jordan: Looking at ELB metrics — currently stable, unhealthy count trending to 0. Backend pod restarts showed a couple OOMKilled before rollback; memory bump deployed to canary earlier but we reverted.
emily: Verified application logs show larger request spikes leading to memory pressure on a subset of pods in us-west-2b. We've scaled replicas in other AZs by +30% and increased node pool temporarily.
yuki: I'm opening a ticket with the cloud provider — host-level NIC errors on a subset of instances suspicious (kernel-level netflap). Putting this in provider ticket with packet captures and instance ids.
sam: Customer impact: about 4% of US-West traffic experienced errors during the peak; top-level impact window ~5m. We're continuing watch.
claire: Drafted status update for customers and posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1975550123
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled in 25m to @yuki (next oncall).
sam: Handing off to yuki — I'm marking incident as mitigated for now, will stay available for escalation. Please keep an eye on Route53 health-check flaps and ELB target counts.
yuki: Taking over monitoring for 1h watch. I'll follow up in ticket with provider and record root cause candidates.
emily: (reacted with :eyes:) continuing to monitor logs and metrics; will update if error rate climbs above 1%.
sam: Thanks team — great fast work. Leaving the channel to yuki. :thumbsup:
